claims.text: Laser cladding with a tailored HEA coating can restore a damaged high-value component.
Laser-cladding repair avoids the hot-cracking problems typical of fusion-welding repair.
The repaired component will maintain service performance under aggressive operating conditions.
The component alloy's microstructure and thermal properties predispose it to hot cracking during conventional fusion-welding repair.
A FeCrNiTiZr-based HEA coating can be deposited as the repair layer.
The FeCrNiTiZr-based HEA can be optimized to form a refined single-phase microstructure with controlled grain size.
The relevant service environment includes elevated temperatures and severe thermal cycling comparable to hot-working or high-temperature tooling.
Laser cladding produces a narrow heat-affected zone with minimal dilution.
Minimal dilution produces a homogeneous, crack-resistant microstructure that acts as a protective surface layer.
Laser cladding provides lower heat input and more rapid solidification than traditional fusion-welding repair.
Lower heat input and rapid solidification suppress liquation and solidification cracking.
Tailored HEA chemistry minimizes the formation of low-melting secondary phases.
Tailored HEA chemistry refines the grain structure.
The tailored HEA chemistry enhances elevated-temperature wear resistance.
The proposed repair enhances fatigue resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
Under identical thermal loading and aggressive service conditions, laser-clad repairs will have significantly less hot cracking than fusion-welded repairs.
Laser-clad repairs will have longer fatigue life than fusion-welded repairs.
Laser-clad repairs will retain better overall microstructural integrity than fusion-welded repairs.
Traditional fusion-welding repair typically causes pronounced hot cracking and microstructural degradation under aggressive operating conditions.
A FeCrNiTiZr HEA coating with high hardness and elevated-temperature wear resistance is reported as a suitable repair material for H13 hot-working tool steel.
